thread:
karim_sales: Quick Q from Acme POC — they need to preserve client source IP to an on‑prem app behind their firewall. We're exploring PrivateLink vs an SNI/HTTP proxy vs VPC peering. What exact questions should we ask their net team and what are the firewall allowlist entries they need for a minimal POC? Also they want clarity on cost impact for PrivateLink vs proxy. cc @maria_netops

maria_netops: Short version: PrivateLink (Interface Endpoint) does NOT preserve original client IP to our service — traffic to the provider shows as the endpoint ENI IPs. So if they require true source IP preservation, PrivateLink alone won't do it. Options below.

ben_sre: +1. Options to consider:
• Outbound model (customer initiates connection to hosted API) — preserves client IP. Easy for firewall allowlist.
• Reverse proxy in their VPC that forwards X-Forwarded-For — preserves in headers but not TCP source IP. Good for logs/routing, not for IP-based mTLS auth.
• Peering with our VPC (only for private deployments where peering is allowed) — can preserve src IP if traffic is routed without SNAT, but peering has scale/ACL tradeoffs.
• PrivateLink + BYOIP/EIP mapping on our side or static proxy EIPs — possible but requires mapping & ops.

elaine_eng: From the runtime side: we can consume X-Forwarded-For and use it in telemetry and routing rules, but we cannot use an XFF header as a cryptographic identity. If customer requires client cert validation by IP/CN, you need a TCP passthrough / mTLS termination that preserves socket info.

karim_sales: Got it. Can someone paste a minimal firewall allowlist and callout for TLS inspect / SNI behavior we can hand to their net team? Also note any fields we should fill in on their security questionnaire (e.g., inbound ports, cert requirements).

maria_netops: Minimal POC allowlist (customer outbound):
- Allow TCP 443 to our service endpoints (if using hosted API or proxy). We'll provide either ENI CIDRs or public EIPs depending on deployment.
- Allow outbound UDP/TCP 53 to their DNS resolver (or allow DNS proxy to resolve Redwood hostnames).
- Allow UDP 123 to NTP if strict time sync required.
- Optional: allow outbound 80 for health checks / redirects (not required if you use HTTPS).

TLS/SNI notes:
- If the customer does TLS inspect, SNI may be altered and certificate pinning can break — recommend creating an egress bypass for redwood domains or use a dedicated egress proxy that preserves TLS.
- If they want client IP preserved for logging: use a cust-side proxy that inserts X-Forwarded-For and whitelists that header; we can log it but not rely on it for auth.

ben_sre: Example SG/ACL snippet they can paste into AWS Security Group UI:

"""
# Customer SG - outbound rules
Type: HTTPS
Protocol: TCP
Port range: 443
Destination: <REPLACE_WITH_REDWOOD_ENDPOINT_CIDRS_OR_EIPS>
Description: allow outbound HTTPS to Redwood POC endpoints

Type: NTP
Protocol: UDP
Port range: 123
Destination: 0.0.0.0/0 (or internal NTP)
"""

ben_sre: We'll provide the CIDR list once you confirm POC deployment mode. If using PrivateLink we provide ENI CIDRs; if using dedicated proxy we provide EIPs.

elaine_eng: Pricing/ops callouts for sales:
- PrivateLink: AWS charges data processing + you pay for interface endpoints. We may also bill for Private connectivity in Dedicated/Private plans if there's non-trivial egress.
- Proxy/EIP model: customer egress to our public EIPs -> normal hosted per‑token pricing applies; network cost depends on cloud egress (we absorb or pass-through depending on contract).
- Peering: typically part of Private deployments; licencing/commit terms apply (talk to finance/AE for quoting).

sam_sales: I'll loop in finance for a quick POC credit and pricing delta. Karim — can you capture expected RPS, avg tokens per request, and whether they need client-IP for auth (not just logging)?

karim_sales: Yep — will get RPS + avg seq length today and confirm if auth by IP is a hard blocker.

deploybot: INFO: provisional ENI ranges for PrivateLink POC: 10.248.50.0/24, 10.248.51.0/24 — these are subject to change. If you need stable EIPs request a static proxy allocation via @netops.

maria_netops: Also ask their net team:
- Are they doing TLS inspect / outbound proxy?
- Do they require mTLS with source IP binding?
- Can they accept X-Forwarded-For or do they need raw TCP source IP?
- Do they prefer inbound (our side) peering or outbound (their side) connections?

ben_sre: Next steps:
1) Karim: confirm desired flow (PrivateLink vs proxy vs peering) and RPS/tokens.
2) We (netops+SRE) will provide final ENI/EIP list and SG snippet.
3) Sales/finance will draft a short POC pricing note (credits / egress).
4) Security Qs: fill in 'We do not require client IP for auth unless configured — XFF supported' (we'll draft the exact phrase if you want).

karim_sales: Perfect — I'll send to customer now. Thx everyone :thumbsup:
